countries.summary: Alberta's regulator denied Synapse Real Estate Corp.'s application for a 1,400 MW gas-fired power plant to serve a data centre campus at Olds, finding the site too close to homes; the decision (Decision 30732-D01-2026, 18 Aug 2026) says it is not a view on data centres as such. Alberta's Bill 12 proposes a levy of up to 2% on computer equipment for data centres of 75 MW or more. Québec's authorization threshold of 5 MW is under challenge in Hydro-Québec's R-4333-2026 tariff file, where intervenors argue a 4.9 MW split would avoid ministerial review.

countries.summary: Chile's Quilicura commune hosts Google's Chile data centre, which Google says is the first in Latin America. In early 2026 residents of Quilicura ran a one-day 'Quili.AI' action, organised by the NGO Corporación Ngen, to draw attention to the water used by AI. Google reports 92% hourly carbon-free energy at Quilicura for 2024 and says its investments in Chile supported about 5,520 jobs a year (2021-2023 averages).

countries.summary: Stockholm's Kista district has a new 30 MW atNorth site (SWE02) that is designed to recover heat into the local district heating system in collaboration with Stockholm Exergi. The Stockholm mayor publicly welcomed the site as a contribution to the city's climate efforts. The site's go-live is scheduled for Q4 2027.

atNorth's FIN02 data centre in Espoo (Sinimäki) recovers waste heat for the neighbouring Kesko store, which the company says will cover almost all of that site's heating energy. atNorth also reports a 45 MW power access agreement with Caruna Espoo Oy.

In Attica, the Spata-Artemida municipal council gave a negative opinion on the environmental impact study for an 80 MW data centre planned by Dromeus Capital and APTO, and residents have appealed to the Council of State. Attica's regional council is the body that rules on the study; this pass verified the municipal opinion and the resident appeal but not the regional decision.

Microsoft's Kemps Creek data centre in Penrith LGA (SSD-10101987) was approved under NSW State Significant Development on 13 July 2023 according to the NSW Planning Portal. Penrith City Council's own page (January 2022) gave the applicant's jobs estimate and said the assessment was then with the NSW Government.

fields.title: Alberta data centre levy (Bill 12, Financial Statutes Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025) amending the Alberta Corporate Tax Act
fields.summary: The government fact sheet describes a levy of up to 2% on the value of computer equipment for data centres of 75 MW or more, with a lower rate for sites that bring their own power generation. The levy is deductible from Alberta corporate income tax. Law-firm summaries state Royal Assent in December 2025 and an effective date of 31 December 2026, but those dates were not confirmed on an official page, so the status is kept at proposed.
key_terms: Introduce a levy of up to two per cent on the value of computer equipment for large data centres (with 75 megawatts of power or more).

fields.title: Kemps Creek data centre, Penrith LGA (SSD-10101987): Microsoft state significant development
fields.summary: NSW Department of Planning approved the state significant development for the Kemps Creek data centre (decision 'Approved', determination 13/07/2023). The approval is for construction and operation of a data centre with two data-storage buildings, 61 generators, a substation, a high-voltage switchyard and 30 diesel storage tanks.
key_terms: Construction and Operation of a Data Centre including two data storage buildings, 61 generators, substation, high voltage switch yard, 30 diesel storage tanks

records.source_title: NSW Planning Portal — Kemps Creek Data Centre (SSD-10101987)
records.notes: Probed HIT on the portal's record fields. This is a planning approval, not a community benefit agreement, so it is recorded as a regulation with status in_effect. The instrument is the state's decision. Currency is inferred as AUD from the NSW context of the council page, which printed '$'. The value is the capital investment value as stated by the council page, not a verified commitment. The 'in_effect' status says the approval stands; construction is not confirmed. The planning portal lists the development as 'Approved', with the decision on the record; the 'over $300 million' figure is from Penrith council's January 2022 page.
